calls.head: Carolina shoots from the point; Florida works down low
calls.body: On point-shot reliance, Carolina sits 5th of 32, at the point-heavy end of the scale. Florida is 29th, at the down low end.
calls.call: Carolina takes a bigger share of its shots from the point than Florida.

calls.head: Depth against star power
calls.body: On depth, Carolina sits 1st of 32, at the deep end of the scale. Florida is 18th, at the top-heavy end.

CAR.head: We gave Carolina a 68% chance, but Florida had other ideas.

FLA.head: We gave Florida a 32% chance, and Florida proved us wrong.

surprises.head: Florida brought the hits
surprises.body: Florida’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 257, against its usual 122 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 600 games.

surprises.head: Florida flipped the shot count
surprises.body: Florida took 65% of the 5-on-5 shot attempts (adjusted for score and venue). From how these two usually play, Florida would expect about 42%. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 900 games.

surprises.head: Carolina shut down Florida’s power play
surprises.body: Florida’s power play created 2.3 expected goals per 60, against its usual 8.0 and a league average of 7.6. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 35 games.

surprises.head: J. Markstrom stole one
surprises.body: J. Markstrom allowed 0 goals on shots worth 2.5 expected goals, 2.5 fewer than expected. Starting goalies had a night this good about once every 25 starts over the last three seasons.
